description:
Generate images, video, speech, music and sound effects — and transcribe speech — via the AI gateway.

Call with NO arguments first: returns the curated model catalog, every entry tagged with its `capability` (text2image, image2image, text2video, image2video, text2speech, speech2text, …). Filter with `capability`; `source: "all"` (together with a `capability`) adds the provider models — e.g. music and sound effects under `text2audio`.

Then call with `model` + `prompt` (+ optional `format` aspect like "16:9"). Model-specific inputs (duration, voice, lyrics, an input file…) go in `params`, sent to the model verbatim under the model's own field names — `model` + `schema: true` returns the fields a model takes. A `uri` inside `params` that an earlier tool result gave you is uploaded for the model first (e.g. `{ audio_url: '<id>' }` to transcribe).

For image-to-image, pass `image_uris` with uris an earlier tool result gave you. Never assemble one by hand.

Returns ONE JSON part: the asset, in the engine's own asset shape — `{ id, meta: { uri, mimeType, kind, duration?, width?, height?, thumbUri? } }`, the same objects `asset_search` returns, plus `cost` (credits) when the gateway reports it. `id` is the durable handle: embed it in `edit` code (image or video fill, audio block) and pass it back here as an `image_uris` entry. It equals `meta.uri`. `meta.kind` is `image`, `video`, `audio` or `file`; `meta.duration` (seconds, as a string) is present for audio/video when the file header states it. Any other result that is data rather than a file comes back as `{ output }`, verbatim.

Transcription (speech2text, e.g. `elevenlabs/scribe-v2`): put the recording's uri in the model's audio field (`audio_url`) — audio OR video of any length; the audio is extracted and long recordings are split for you. The result is `{ transcriptUri, duration, language?, wordCount, lines }`: `lines` holds one `[mm:ss.s–mm:ss.s] sentence` per sentence (times in the source), enough to pick moments by; the word timings stay in the `transcriptUri` asset — read them inside `edit` with `engine.design.readTranscript(transcriptUri, { from, to })` (words whose start lies in [from, to) seconds), e.g. to build captions.

NO PICTURE COMES BACK. To see what was generated, place it and look at the render `edit` returns: `await engine.design.setProps(blockId, { fill: { type: 'image', uri: '<id>' } })`, or `await engine.design.create({ type: 'graphic', props: { width: 400, height: 400, shape: { type: 'rect' }, fill: { type: 'image', uri: '<id>' } } }, { parent: page })`. That shows it in the layout, which is what you have to judge anyway. Do not assume a generation is good — look before you build on it.

Multi-output models (layerize-class: decompose an input image into layers) add an `assets` array of the same objects, in stack order (residual background first, then cutout layers). The top-level fields ARE `assets[0]`. Single-output results carry no `assets` array. Any non-image output the model produced is passed through VERBATIM under `metadata` — read it, it binds semantics to the assets.

Requires a free IMG.LY sign-in (the `login` tool); all other design tools work without an account.

image_uris.description: Uris returned by `import` or an earlier `asset_generate`, used as inputs (image-to-image models).

model.description: Model id from the catalog (call with no arguments to list). Required to generate or to read a schema.

params.description: Model-specific inputs sent verbatim (e.g. { "voice": "Aria" }, { "duration": 8 }). Asset uris inside are uploaded first.

prompt.description: What to generate. Required with `model` unless the model takes its input through `params`.

schema.description: With `model`: return that model's input schema instead of generating.

source.description: Catalog source: "catalog" (default, curated) or "all" (adds the provider models; needs `capability`).

name: asset_generate
